Independent School in Berkshire
Choosing the right school is about more than academic success. Families exploring private schools in Berkshire are often looking for a school that combines strong results with individual support, excellent pastoral care and opportunities that prepare students for life beyond the classroom.
Located in Ascot, Heathfield School is an independent day and boarding school offering a personalised approach to education within a close-knit and ambitious environment. With small class sizes, flexible boarding and a strong focus on student wellbeing, Heathfield provides an education designed to help every student grow in confidence and achieve their potential.
For families considering private education in Berkshire, Heathfield offers the advantages of a well-connected location, a supportive community and a broad educational experience that balances academic achievement with personal development.
A Leading Private School in Berkshire
Among independent schools in Berkshire, Heathfield is recognised for its highly individual approach. The school’s intentionally smaller size allows teachers and pastoral staff to know every student personally, creating an environment where students are both supported and challenged.
Small class sizes encourage participation, independent thinking and closer relationships between students and teachers. This personalised approach enables staff to adapt teaching and support to each student’s strengths, interests and ambitions.
Academic achievement is supported by a broad co-curricular programme that encourages students to develop confidence beyond the classroom. Whether through sport, creative arts, leadership opportunities or enrichment activities, students are encouraged to explore their interests and build skills that will support them throughout life.
For many families searching for private schools in Berkshire, Heathfield offers an appealing balance of academic ambition, pastoral support and individual attention.
Boarding School Opportunities in Berkshire
Boarding remains a central part of the Heathfield experience. The school offers full, weekly and flexible boarding options designed to meet the needs of modern families, including those based in London, across the UK and internationally.
The boarding environment is structured, welcoming and supportive, helping students develop independence while benefiting from consistent pastoral care and supervision. Students build strong friendships within a close-knit boarding community and benefit from a balanced routine of study, activities and downtime.
Flexible boarding can also provide practical advantages for busy families, allowing students to participate fully in school life while maintaining strong family connections. For families researching boarding schools in Berkshire, Heathfield combines the reassurance of strong pastoral support with the opportunities and independence that boarding can offer.
Sixth Form Preparation for University and Beyond
Heathfield’s Sixth Form is designed to prepare students for university, careers and adult life through a combination of academic focus and personal development.
Students benefit from small A Level classes, personalised support from teachers and tailored university preparation. Dedicated Sixth Form facilities provide space for independent study, collaboration and leadership development within a more mature learning environment.
Alongside academic study, students are encouraged to develop confidence, communication skills and independence through leadership roles, enrichment opportunities and wider school involvement.
From September 2026, Heathfield’s Sixth Form will become co-educational, further strengthening the school’s dynamic and forward-looking approach while maintaining its established culture of individual support. For families considering private sixth forms in Berkshire, Heathfield offers a supportive environment that helps students prepare confidently for the next stage of their education.
Excellent Accessibility from London
For many families, location is an important factor when comparing private schools near London. Heathfield’s Ascot location offers the advantages of a Berkshire school setting while remaining highly accessible from the capital and surrounding counties.
The school is within easy reach of Central London, Heathrow Airport, Surrey, Buckinghamshire and Hampshire, making travel straightforward for day students, weekly boarders and visiting families. This accessibility allows families to benefit from a spacious and secure school environment without feeling disconnected from London. For boarding families in particular, the combination of strong transport links and a countryside setting can offer the best of both worlds.
A Clear and Supportive Admissions Process
Heathfield’s admissions process is designed to be personal, transparent and supportive from the first enquiry onwards. Families are encouraged to visit the school to experience the community, meet staff and students and gain a clear understanding of daily life at Heathfield.
The admissions team works closely with prospective families throughout each stage of the process, whether they are considering day places, boarding or Sixth Form entry.
Entry points include 11+, 13+ and Sixth Form, with assessments and interviews designed to identify students who will thrive within the school’s academic and pastoral environment. For families relocating to Berkshire or considering boarding for the first time, personalised guidance throughout the admissions journey can make an important difference.
Outstanding Pastoral Care and Student Support
Pastoral care is central to the Heathfield experience. Students are supported by tutors, boarding staff, Heads of Year and senior pastoral leaders who know them individually and provide consistent support throughout school life.
The school’s smaller size allows staff to recognise strengths, monitor wellbeing closely and identify concerns early. Students are encouraged to develop resilience, confidence and independence within a caring and structured environment.
Strong pastoral support is particularly important within boarding life, where creating a genuine sense of belonging and community is essential. Heathfield’s supportive culture helps students feel secure, valued and fully involved in school life.
FAQ
What are the benefits of attending a private school in Berkshire?
Berkshire is home to some of the UK’s most respected independent schools, offering strong academic standards, extensive co-curricular opportunities and excellent facilities. Families often choose private education in Berkshire for its combination of academic ambition, individual support and convenient access to London and the South East. At Heathfield, students benefit from small class sizes, personalised teaching and a nurturing environment where they are known and supported as individuals.
Is Heathfield School a boarding school in Berkshire?
Yes. Heathfield is a leading independent boarding and day school in Berkshire. Boarding is an integral part of school life, helping students develop independence, confidence and lasting friendships within a supportive community. Flexible boarding options are also available to meet the needs of modern families.
Is Heathfield School near London?
Yes. Heathfield School is located in Ascot, Berkshire, approximately 50 minutes from central London by train. The school’s location offers the best of both worlds: a peaceful and spacious setting in the Berkshire countryside, with excellent transport connections to London, Heathrow Airport and the wider South East.
Does Heathfield offer Sixth Form education?
Yes. Heathfield offers a dedicated Sixth Form experience designed to prepare students for university and future careers. Students benefit from small A Level classes, personalised academic support, leadership opportunities and access to the purpose-built Cadogan Sixth Form Centre. From September 2026, Heathfield’s Sixth Form is becoming co-educational, creating an even broader and more dynamic learning environment.
Why do families choose Heathfield School?
Families choose Heathfield because of its distinctive combination of academic excellence, exceptional pastoral care and strong sense of community. Students are encouraged to be ambitious, develop confidence and embrace opportunities both inside and outside the classroom. The school’s Ascot location, boarding provision, individual approach and future-focused Sixth Form offering make it a popular choice for families seeking an independent school in Berkshire.

About Us
Heathfield is an intentionally small school for girls aged 11-18 years which offers day and boarding places. We are delighted that from September 2026, our Sixth Form will become co-educational, welcoming boys for the first time in our history. This extension will create new and exciting benefits for all students, providing a rich academic and social experience and bringing diverse perspectives and collaboration across productions, clubs and student leadership. Our Sixth Form students will gain invaluable experience in a mixed environment, equipping them with the confidence, skills and resilience to thrive in future co-educational settings.
With a reputation for excellence in pastoral care, every student is known at Heathfield. The School encourages a positive, adventurous mindset, inspiring students to embrace new challenges and explore diverse interests. Heathfield provides boundless opportunities ensuring every student can confidently step into uncharted territories, discovering and cultivating their passions in an environment that celebrates both individuality and collective growth.
With the development of confidence and self-belief, each student is empowered to positively navigate their own academic and personal journey. Life in the 21st century demands resilience and adaptability; we aim to equip our students with both academic qualifications and life skills.
The boarding ethos is central to the Heathfield community and benefits both boarders and day students alike. Boarding comes with a built-in social life and enables the development of close and life-long friendships. Living and working together teaches empathy, respect, independence and self-confidence.
The 24/7 boarding environment provides the ultimate in flexibility for day students who can be dropped off as early as 7.30am for breakfast. Pick up time is from 4pm, although day students tend to stay on for co-curricular and extra-curricular activities, sport and supervised prep. We understand that arrangements can often change last minute, so day students can be collected up to 9pm when they will have completed their activities, prep, had their supper and enjoyed some down time with their friends.
Weekends are filled with a busy, diverse and well-structured age-appropriate programme of fun activities ranging from Indoor Skydiving, Segways and Zorbing to Mountain Biking, Ice Skating and Rock Climbing. Students also enjoy socials with local boys schools including Eton and Papplewick, along with trips to the theatre, cinema, shopping centres and water parks, as well as on site activities such as Cooking, Arts & Crafts and whole School House events.
To find out more, please arrange to visit us by contacting Admissions on 01344 898342, thank you.
History
The school stands in 36 acres of grounds on the outskirts of Ascot and has done so since Heathfield School was founded in 1899 by Eleanor Beatrice Wyatt, its first headmistress. In 1882, at the age of 24, Miss Wyatt and her mother opened a mixed school in Drayton Gardens, South Kensington, then in 1884, as the school expanded, moved to 45 Stanhope Gardens. Still a mixed school (though the numbers of girls by now far exceeded those of the boys), its popularity continued to increase necessitating a move in 1891 to 132 and latterly also 133 Queens Gate.
Until this point Miss Wyatt had been concentrating on educating boys and girls from the lower-middle and lower classes; however, she was convinced that the best way to further education for all was to educate those who could in turn educate others. This coincided with Miss Wyatt’s desire to move out of a congested and claustrophobic London. The problem she faced was that, whilst wishing to move to a more spacious country location, she still wanted to maintain a proximity to London and the school’s active Old Girl network. In 1899 the perfect solution was found in the leafy environs of Berkshire and Heathfield School was founded in what was a beautiful Italianate building, the original home of the Paravacini family. On the 8th of May the school was officially opened and the chapel blessed.
Some years previously, and far from the bustle of London, Reverend W J Butler became Vicar of Wantage on 1 January 1847. His main aims were, first to revive the religious life in England and second to improve education. He hoped to achieve these aims by setting up an Order of Teaching Sisters but he faced many disappointments and spent 25 years trying to improve various day schools in the Parish before St. Mary’s School, Wantage was founded in 1873.
The school was run by the sisters of the Community of St. Mary the Virgin and was based in the Queen Anne house on Newbury Street. Sister Ellen was the first Sister-in-Charge and was later followed by Sister Juliana. Sister Annie Louisa started a guide movement called Scout Patrols in 1899 before Boy Scouts had even begun! She succeeded Sister Juliana as Head Mistress in 1903 and by the time she left in 1919 St. Mary’s was recognised as a “public school with an unusually high standard of scholarship”.
Both Heathfield and St. Mary’s Wantage flourished independently though with almost identical values; each producing some outstanding alumni. In 2006 the two schools merged, with Heathfield incorporating St. Mary’s Wantage onto the Ascot site resulting in a combined school drawing on the outstanding heritage and ethos of both.
Boarding has changed beyond recognition but there are many misconceptions about the meaning of full boarding. Today, flexibility is required to accommodate the many demands and complexities of modern family life. Optional leave weekends are frequent, there are four such weekends in the Michaelmas Term, two in the Lent Term, and three in the Summer Term. Weekly boarding (5 nights per week) was introduced in 2022 and part time boarding (1, 2 or 3 nights per week) in 2023.
Since day students were first admitted to the school in 2015, this option has grown in popularity. Day students are an integral and valued part of the school community with access to all the facilities and activities open to boarders.

Commercial & Venue Hire
With our first-class facilities and ample parking we are able to cater for all manner of events from the smallest of family functions to large scale events requiring whole-school hire.
During the school holidays, Heathfield School is the ideal venue for events – residential camps, team building days, academic and music schools, conferences and private celebrations can all be accommodated.
We boast both historic and 21st century buildings suitable for a range of events, as well as extensive grounds which include grass pitches, and woodlands – all situated in a stunning 36 acre campus. Accommodation for 170 is available in our comfortable boarding houses and there is also space onsite for camping.
The school leisure facilities include a 220 seat theatre, dance studio, digital recording studio, sports hall, fitness suite and heated indoor 25m swimming pool. The pool is ideal for swimming lessons, galas, children’s parties and a range of other water-based activities. The school holds a wedding license and the stunning chapel can be used for both weddings and Christenings. The school’s onsite caterers offer bespoke menus that can be tailored for each event. Ascot and Martins Heron railway stations, less than 2 miles away, have regular direct trains to London Waterloo. Heathrow airport is less than half an hour away and Gatwick airport only 43 miles away.
For more information on hiring our venues, please click on the School Hire link below, or contact the Bursar below.

Heathfield celebrates exceptional GCSE results
There were smiles all round at Heathfield School today as students celebrated an outstanding set of GCSE results, with more than 80% of grades exceeding students’ nationally standardised targets.
The results are a strong reflection of the progress students make at Heathfield, where small classes and a highly personalised approach to learning enable every student to fulfil their potential.
Overall, 64% of all grades were awarded at 9–7, with an impressive 40% of grades at 9–8 (A*).
The breadth and depth of success was showcased across the cohort: 100% of students achieved a pass in both Maths and Science, while more than 40% of students achieved the highest possible grade 9 in English Literature, History and Spanish.
Among the standout individual performances:
The Value Added across the board once again exceeded an average of a full grade per subject per student – and we are immensely proud of all of their accomplishments. Their achievements are testament not only to their hard work and determination, but also to the supportive and personalised education they receive at Heathfield.
Jonathan Williams, Head, said: “I am delighted with this year’s GCSE results and would like to congratulate every student on their excellent achievements. These results are a wonderful reflection of the commitment and determination of our students, alongside the dedication of our teaching staff.
At Heathfield, we believe that an excellent education is about much more than examination results. Our students benefit from a genuinely broad and diverse education, where academic achievement sits alongside success in sport, music, drama and the arts. In our small, supportive community, every student is known, valued and encouraged to aim high and be the very best version of themselves.”
Celebrating A Level success
The majority of grades awarded at A*-B 100% of the cohort secure at least one A*–B grade
Congratulations to all our Upper Sixth students on their A Level results. The majority of grades were awarded at A*–B, with 100% of the cohort securing at least one A*–B grade.
The breadth of academic achievement is particularly impressive, with students studying Art, Classical Civilisation, English Literature, Photography, Politics, Psychology, Spanish and the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) achieving 100% A*–B grades.
These results demonstrate both the academic ambition of Heathfield’s students and the breadth of interests they are encouraged to pursue. This diversity is reflected in their exciting university choices, with degree subjects ranging from Medicine, International Finance, Politics and Marketing & Management to Fine Art and Fashion Contour.
Alongside studying at leading Russell Group universities, Heathfield students are also taking their next steps on an increasingly international stage, with destinations including Madrid, New York, Paris, Rome and Texas.
Behind the many statistics are stories of students who have thrived and given their all at Heathfield, following different pathways that have enabled them to pursue their passions. Esme joined the school in Year 7, and after achieving A*BB in Art, Religious Studies and Sociology, she will continue her creative education at the University of the Arts, London, studying Fashion Contour.
Martha joined Heathfield in Year 9, and after achieving A*A*A in Psychology, Art and Biology, will take up her place at Durham University to study Marketing & Management. Emilia joined Heathfield in the Sixth Form, and after achieving ABB in Spanish, Drama and Art, is looking forward to her next chapter studying Fashion Design in Madrid.
These stories and the breadth of destinations and degree choices reflect the individual aspirations of Heathfield students and the school’s commitment to enabling each young person to identify and pursue their own academic and professional pathway.
Jonathan Williams, Head, said: “We are immensely proud of the academic achievements of this year’s students. Their results are a reflection of their intellectual curiosity, determination and hard work, alongside the outstanding teaching and individual support they receive at Heathfield. It is particularly rewarding to see the breadth of subjects our students are going on to study and the range of universities and destinations they have chosen. We wish each student every success as they embark on this exciting next chapter.”
Heathfield students celebrate outstanding GCSE results

Entry Procedure
In order to be invited for assessment and considered for a place at the school, applicants must first be registered with us. The registration form must be completed and submitted with a £240 (including VAT) registration fee. Please click the button below for the registration form.
Joining Heathfield at 11+
Candidates registered for entry to Heathfield will be assessed in numeracy, literacy and non-verbal ability via the online CEM (Centre for Evaluation and Monitoring) test. The assessment is designed to evaluate potential rather than knowledge, so tutoring and preparation are not required. They will also attend an interview with the Head.
Heathfield aims to make a holistic evaluation of candidates; all components of the assessment together with a reference from the candidate’s current school will be evaluated in order to identify those who will benefit from the many opportunities that the school offers. The aim of the process is to identify potential. We are looking for well-rounded students with a genuine interest in education in the broadest sense of the word, with interests that include and stretch beyond the academic curriculum. The School has strong traditions in academia, art, drama, music, community activities and sport. There are many co-curricular activities, all of which are important in developing a well-balanced, confident and happy individual.
Joining Heathfield at 13+
Candidates registered for entry will be assessed in small groups. Those registered will be allocated a date and time for their assessment and interview.
Please contact admissions@heathfieldschool.net for further information.
Deferred Entry
Candidates seeking entrance at 13+ may also opt to apply for a place at 11+ and defer entry until Form III (Year 9). Such candidates will be assessed in the Autumn Term of Year 6 in the same way as 11+ candidates applying for the following academic year. This enables pupils to remain in 13+ prep schools secure in the knowledge that they have an offer of a place subject to final references.

The School has strong traditions in academia, art, drama, music, community activities and sport. There are many co-curricular activities, all of which are important in developing a well-balanced, confident and happy individual.
Common Entrance
Common Entrance is not a requirement for Heathfield; places are offered based on performance in our assessment and interview.
Joining Heathfield at 16+
Heathfield welcomes applications from all candidates wishing to join our co-ed Sixth Form for A Level study.
Registered Sixth Form candidates will be invited to visit the school for an interview with the Head of Sixth Form. Offers are made conditional on iGCSE/GCSE results, performance at interview and a reference from the current school. Candidates should achieve a minimum of six grades 9-4 (A* – C) with a minimum grade 6 (B) in any subject taken at GCSE that is to be pursued at A Level.
Joining as an International Student
Overseas students are welcomed at Heathfield. Applicants should register with the school and will be invited to the relevant assessment for their year of entry. Where it is not possible for candidates to attend for assessment, they should submit a UKiset profile (see www.ukiset.com for details). An interview with the Head will be conducted via Zoom and assessments for international students also include language testing.
Please click the button below for more details on EAL provision for international students.
Applying for a Visa
Heathfield School is a Highly Trusted Sponsor under the UK Visas & Immigration’s Child Student visa system. We hold a child student visa licence and may sponsor students for their secondary education at the school. In order to provide students with the Confirmation of Acceptance to Study (CAS) required for a visa application, we require payment of a term’s fees and the international deposit, alongside UKVI required guardian details.
On behalf of Heathfield School, Newland Chase Education, an immigration and visas provider with specialised knowledge of the needs of educational institutions and students, will issue the CAS and assist in the Visa application directly with you. Parents are billed directly for this service by Newland Chase Education.
Visas are valid up until the end of the GCSE course. A new CAS is required for the two year A Level programme in the Sixth Form.
If you have any queries regarding visas please contact our Admissions Team.
Guardianship
It is a legal requirement for every student in the UK to have a Guardian. This can be a friend or relative or there are several guardianship agencies which act on parents behalf with a varying level of services. The contract for guardianship is between the parent and the Guardian. The accredited organisation for guardianship is AEGIS and to go to their website for a list of guardianship agencies please click here. http://www.aegisuk.net/
A list of duties that we would normally expect Guardians to undertake please can be found in the School’s Educational Guardianship policy, which is listed here. All Guardians must have UK citizenship or settled status and be over the age of 25.

Scholarships at 11+ and 13+
Heathfield offers Academic, Art, Drama, Music, and Sport Scholarships at 11+ and 13+.
Scholars must demonstrate significant levels of academic, creative, or sporting enthusiasm, achievement and potential. An award carries with it title and prestige and gives the holder access to our scholarship programme to further potential. There is no monetary award or remission of fees. 11+ and 13+ scholarships remain in place until the end of Form V but scholars may re-apply for Sixth Form Scholarships.
Scholars make significant contributions to the school and will develop their skills and potential through support from their personal mentor. 11+ and 13+ subject scholars will be required to follow the relevant subject to GCSE level to retain the scholarship, Sixth Form subject scholars should follow the relevant subject at A Level.
For further information regarding scholarships, please contact admissions@heathfieldschool.net
Sixth Form Scholarships
Heathfield offers Academic, Art, Drama, Music, Photography and Sport Scholarships at 16+. Subject scholars are expected to study the subject of their award at A Level.
For further information regarding scholarships, please contact admissions@heathfieldschool.net
Academic Scholarship
11+ and 13+
An academic scholarship will be awarded to the 11+ applicant who performs highly in all aspects of the assessment and at interview. There will be no separate academic scholarship examination or interview and no application is required.
13+ applicants who wish to apply for an academic scholarship will be invited to attend a lesson following which they will participate in a discussion. They will also sit a one-hour aptitude assessment and attend an interview.
Sixth Form
Candidates are expected to have GCSE predictions of grades 7 and above. They will also sit a one-hour aptitude assessment and attend an interview.
Art Scholarship
Candidates are required to present a portfolio which showcases examples of their work. The portfolio should be presented in any format but be A3 minimum and include up to 20 pages showing a range of processes. If any of the outcomes are digital, these should be presented on a memory stick. The portfolio should be built up of original work and it is also expected that final pieces will be shown alongside any preparatory studies. Applicants are also encouraged to include examples of outside interests, such as gallery visits or extracurricular courses.
Candidates will be invited to undertake a drawing assessment and an image analysis activity. There will also be an interview with the Head of Art for candidates to share their portfolio and to discuss their interests and experiences of Art and Design. 11+ and 13+ scholars are expected to study GCSE Art and Sixth Form scholars should take Art and Design A Level.
Drama Scholarship
Candidates are required to prepare and perform a monologue of their own choosing of 2 minutes maximum. A review of no more than 500 words about a play or performance they have seen in the last year should also be submitted with the application.
Applicants for the Sixth Form Scholarship will also be sent an ‘unseen’ scene from a play and will be expected to prepare an outline of how they would stage the scene with regards to performance, directorial and design ideas in readiness to discuss with the Director or Drama.
There will be an interview with the Director of Drama; candidates will also participate in a mixed age workshop. 11+ and 13+ applicants are expected to study GCSE Drama and Sixth Form applicants should be taking Drama and Theatre A Level.
Music Scholarship
11+ candidates are required to perform a sight-reading test and play either two instruments (at least one to be at Grade I) or sing and play one instrument (at Grade I). 13+ candidates are required to perform a sight-reading test and play two instruments (at least one to be at Grade III) or sing and play one instrument (at Grade III). At Sixth Form Music/Choral scholarships are awarded to outstanding musicians who play an instrument or sing with exceptional ability (at Grade V). There will also be an interview with the Director of Music.
11+ and 13+ applicants are expected to study GCSE Music and Sixth Form applicants should be taking Music A Level.
Sports Scholarship
Candidates must demonstrate exceptional ability in one or more of the school’s main sports (netball, lacrosse, swimming, athletics, tennis, and cricket) or outstanding ability in another sport. They will be assessed through a variety of physical fitness and endurance tests as well as a game-based activity to assess decision making, communication and teamwork. There will also be an interview with the Director of Sport.
11+ and 13+ applicants are expected to study GCSE PE and Sixth Form applicants should be taking PE A Level.
Photography Scholarship
Sixth Form
Candidates are required to submit a small portfolio of 4-6 photographs they have taken themselves and 1-2 photographs that they like by other photographers. Candidates will be required to provide analytical comment on these images in an interview with the Head of Photography. Applicants should be taking Photography A Level.

Drama
The study of Drama and Theatre Studies plays a significant role in the creative academic and pastoral aspects of our student’s development here at Heathfield. Based in St Mary’s Theatre, Drama lessons for all year groups take place in the auditorium, with smaller classes and LAMDA lessons making use of a smaller, more intimate studio space. Students from all year groups are involved in all aspects of technical theatre, from the programming and rigging of lights and sound engineering training, to stage management skills, costume creation and set building.
All students are encouraged to take part in a diverse extra-curricular programme. Students in Forms I to III perform in the nationwide Shakespeare for Schools Festival, where the cast create and perform an abridged adaptation of a Shakespeare play which is performed at nearby South Hill Park, in the Wilde Theatre. The experience provides our younger students with the opportunity to work with professional actors whilst in the rehearsal period of their production and perform in a professional theatre. Additionally, our Drama Scholars run a weekly lunchtime club for Form I, and our theatre technician offers Technical Theatre Club fortnightly for all year groups. Students work with our resident Theatre Technician on the rigging, plotting, and programming of lights, the detailed creation of soundscape and special effects and the organisation skills involved in stage management.
There are two annual productions, which rotate from a musical and straight play, which students from Form III upwards can take part in, and the Lower School (Forms I to II) perform in a Summer Showcase. Recent productions have included: Shakespeare’s Macbeth, The Addams Family Musical, Sweet Charity and Oliver! Our most recent Showcase was Hans Christian Anderson’s fairy tales, and the new academic year promises more exciting performances, with auditions soon to be held for next year’s musical. Other regular performances include GCSE and A Level Devised pieces created entirely by the students, and scripted performances at both levels where the students direct each other.
In addition to LAMDA throughout Heathfield, our Scholarship programme allows the students to add to their already growing portfolio, through participation in the RADA Shakespeare Certificate. The Certificate requires an enhanced understanding of Shakespeare’s work, performing monologues and duologues which are examined by staff at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art. Scholars are also given opportunities to work with industry professionals and are regularly taken to the theatre, both locally and in the West End. Recent visits from practitioners and performers have included West End Producer and Director, Jonathan Church, Olivier award-winning actress Joanna Riding, and actor Jonjo O’Neill. Our Sixth Form students have also had the opportunity to create an immersive performance with guidance from performers from Punchdrunk Theatre Company.
We regularly take our students on trips to both West End regional theatre productions and we recently joined with the school Choir on a theatrical enrichment trip to New York where, whilst the Choir were singing at a number of exciting venues in the city, Drama students spent a busy week seeing Broadway shows, visiting an award-winning immersive theatre production, and meeting with Broadway Producer Manny Azenberg, and Artistic Director Jill Rafson for a fascinating insight into the workings of the industry. A successful trip that we plan to continue.
We are a bustling and busy department with something always on the go!

Music
Music is a particular strength at Heathfield and the opportunities for experienced and novice musicians and singers are extensive.
We have a Senior Choir for Form III upwards, a Junior Choir for Forms I and II, an Orchestra, a Woodwind Ensemble, a Brass Ensemble, an A Cappella Group and a Band. Students of all standards are welcomed and there is a busy concert schedule, providing all students with opportunities for public performance. The music department has a state of the art 24 track digital recording studio including iMacs and numerous music practice rooms.
Alongside curriculum music lessons, which all students take in Forms I – III, students can also learn one or more musical instruments, and many have individual singing lessons with specialist instrument and voice teachers. We also provide an impressive range of lessons taught by visiting peripatetic teachers. These include the piano, guitar, strings, woodwind, brass, percussion and the harp; students are encouraged to take music examinations and involve themselves with the different orchestras and musical groups on offer. ABRSM (Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music) exams and Trinity College London music exams are offered and students are supported in preparing for and taking these exams.
The Choir enjoy a biennial European tour.

Academic Ethos
The academic life of a school is not just the learning that takes place in class but the breadth and depth of activities both in and out of the classroom. Heathfield is renowned for its strong and vibrant creative and dramatic tradition. What is not so well known is that we are also an academically ambitious and rigorous school, where we prepare our students for careers which have not yet been discovered. Therefore it is vital that our curriculum is skill based as well as ensuring that every student has the relevant academic qualifications to progress onwards to their own particular future goals.
The size of our school means that every student is known which enables our dedicated and talented teachers to engage and motivate every single student. Small class sizes and individual teaching boosts achievement. Heathfield students benefit from a remarkable 4 : 1 student-teacher ratio. Personalised learning plans and performance monitoring help staff and students to analyse progress.
At the heart of what we do is the ability to add value to every student’s education. Value Added is a score produced by the Centre for Evaluation and Monitoring at Durham University, which analyse subject performance and student ability data. For example, our average value added at GCSE was 1.2 (2025 results) of a grade above MidYIS baseline. We cater for all, be they Highly Able, with a Special Educational Need or Disability, with English as an Additional Language or none of these. We celebrate the success of all and do so often with students regularly given public recognition for their achievement with Highflyer and Progress Awards.

School Transport
Situated in the Royal County of Berkshire, just 45 minutes from Central London and 30 minutes from London Heathrow Airport, Heathfield is easily accessible for local, London and international families.
Heathfield School transport is provided by a professional and dedicated team of trained minibus drivers who are proud of the service they provide and would like to welcome your child on-board.
Heathfield’s minibus fleet is modern and comfortable; the buses are operated and maintained under current legislation and all our drivers have enhanced DBS clearance and a clean driving licence.
We look carefully at the annual routes each Summer and the viability of each route is dependent on the number of students that use the service, although we are always happy to discuss alternative or additional routes and pick up points with parents who would like their child to travel to school by bus.

Routes
Daily Mini Bus Service
Heathfield currently operates eight daily local transport routes:
Route 1 – Bourne End, Cookham, Taplow, Maidenhead, Bray
Route 2 – Hammersmith, South Kensington
Route 4 – Langley, Datchet, Wraysbury, Virginia Water, Wentworth, Sunningdale, Ascot
Route 5 – Kingston Vale, Richmond
Route 6 – Farnham Common, Eton, Windsor, Oakley Green
Route 7 – Shinfield, Wokingham
Route 8 – Henley, Hurley, Maidenhead, Warfield
If you would like to discuss the possibility of an additional stop to be added or a new route to be created, contact the Bursar.
The buses arrive at Heathfield by 8am each day and leave Ascot after clubs, activities and prep at 5.30pm Monday – Thursday and 4.15pm on a Friday.
Weekly London Mini Bus Service
Heathfield also operates a convenient weekly transport service to and from Central London for Boarders going home for the weekend.
Students leave school at 4:15pm on Friday evening. Currently, the bus drops off in Chiswick, Hammersmith and South Kensington. The return journey, on Sunday evening, leaves South Kensington at 6:15pm, with stops in Hammersmith and Chiswick and arrives at school around 7:30pm.
Please note timings are approximate and subject to traffic.
The associated cost is £25 per journey.
Application to join our service
If you would like to reserve a seat on one of our daily minibuses for your child (children) please email transport@heathfieldschool.net.
This is an indication of interest and not a firm booking; one term’s bus charge payment must be made in advance to secure a seat for your child. This can be added to your termly bill or paid by BACS transfer (if joining the route after the start of term).
Parents of students whose siblings already use the Heathfield mini bus service must also complete the forms.
Bookings are only accepted for the whole term – not part thereof.
Once we have received all relevant forms, we will be able to process your application and confirm your child’s seat via email.
Cancellation
Please note that half a term’s notice must be given to cancel your season ticket.
Receive more information on the minibus service by emailing transport@heathfieldschool.net
Emergency contact numbers
Each minibus has a dedicated mobile phone on which messages can be left for the driver.
Transport Coordinator’s email: transport@heathfieldschool.net

Community
All Heathfield students are encouraged to consider ways that they can contribute to both the local and international communities as well as the school community. All students are actively involved in a wide variety of volunteering activities, partnerships and fundraising events, both large and small.
Heathfield has a strong link with the Oscar Foundation who visited us in 2018 and 2023. Students raised funds to fly fifteen girls from the Mumbai slums to the UK for a life-changing two-week sport and education tour. The OSCAR Foundation drives social change by encouraging gender equality in underprivileged communities through football and education. The link continues with visits by the Founder of Oscar and with students going to Mumbai to volunteer.
In addition to supporting and fundraising for our four House charities, students also support two additional charities, selected every year. All of these charities are nominated by the students and include a mix of local, national and international causes. Our main annual, student led fundraising event, St Nicholas Stalls, is hugely successful and is a great start to students’ fundraising efforts.
Students have also connected with the residents of Dormy House care home in Sunningdale, corresponding with them throughout the pandemic and beyond.
